newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's No. 2 phone co seeks international partner.
newsitem.headline: Japan's No. 2 phone co seeks international partner.

text.p: Japan's second biggest telephone operator, DDI Corp, said on Tuesday that it is looking for alliances with domestic or foreign carriers, but that telecoms titan NTT appears to be first in line.

"Foreign telecoms firms seem to prefer to wait until they confirm what kind of alliance NTT will make," DDI president Yusai Okuyama told Reuters in an interview. "They are keen to see whether NTT will be in a friendly relationship with them or will become a big competitor."

DDI, which offers domestic long-distance and mobile phone services, has been in talks with both domestic and foreign telecoms operators over a possible tie-up, but no conclusion has yet been made, the president said.
"It would be hard to start international services on our own. We may need to seek some tie-ups," Okuyama said.

Rumours have swirled over the past couple of months about which foreign carrier would court the nation's giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) for a foothold in the lucrative Japanese communications market.
British Telecommunications Plc has so far been seen as the front runner in the race and has been openly seeking an alliance with the Japanese carrier.

In January, the Financial Times said in unsourced article that NTT was exploring a $500 million investment alongside BT in the French telecoms operator Cegetel, which is set up by Cie Generale des Eaux.
NTT has declined to confirm any of the talk, but has only said that there were many such investment proposals.

Japan, whose 15.6 percent share of global revenues makes it the world's third largest telecoms market, agreed last month to remove its 33 percent ceiling on foreign investment in most carriers and radio-based services.

"It is not that we are particularly fascinated with the global market," Okuyama said. "But if we go it alone, we would not be able to provide our customers with the services they need, and it will result in a loss of competitiveness."
The DDI president said the company also aims to start offering local call services as early as next fiscal year in areas close to major cities, where there should be good demand.
For the year ending March 31, Okuyama said that DDI would likely enjoy a record parent current profit exceeding its earlier estimate of 60 billion yen ($491 million).
The company will announce an upward revision in its 1996/97 earnings estimate later this week, he said.

He said its mobile phone business will be a key source of revenue in coming years. The number of DDI mobile phone system subscribers is expected to grow to 10 million by March 1999 from the current level of around six million, he said. ($1=122 yen)
